pages.quiz:
PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Circular motion? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Circular motion.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Circular motion.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Circular motion.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Photoelectric effect? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Photoelectric effect.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Photoelectric effect.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Photoelectric effect.

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Dynamics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Dynamics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Dynamics.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Dynamics.

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electromagnetic induction? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electromagnetic induction.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electromagnetic induction.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electromagnetic induction.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Electromagnetic induction.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Quantity of Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Quantity of Heat.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Quantity of Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Quantity of Heat.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Quantity of Heat.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Photoelectric effect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Electromagnetic induction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Mains electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Transistors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.

2. B — Glucose and oxygen

3. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. B — 100 °C

5. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.

8. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.

10. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electromagnetic induction.

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Quantity of Heat.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Photoelectric effect; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Electromagnetic induction; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Mains electricity; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Transistors; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
